system: mixed system of Portuguese civil law and customary law

constitution.history: previous 1975, 1990; latest adopted 16 November 2004, effective 21 December 2004
constitution.amend: proposed by the president of the republic or supported by at least one third of the Assembly of the Republic membership; passage of amendments affecting constitutional provisions, including the independence and sovereignty of the state, the republican form of government, basic rights and freedoms, and universal suffrage, requires at least a two-thirds majority vote by the Assembly and approval in a referendum; referenda not required for passage of other amendments

courts.highest: Supreme Court (consists of the court president, vice president, and 5 judges); Constitutional Council (consists of 7 judges)
courts.judges: Supreme Court president appointed by the president of the republic; vice president appointed by the president in consultation with the Higher Council of the Judiciary (CSMJ) and ratified by the Assembly of the Republic; other judges elected by the Assembly; judges serve 5-year renewable terms; Constitutional Council judges appointed - 1 by the president, 5 by the Assembly, and 1 by the CSMJ; judges serve 5-year nonrenewable terms
courts.lower: Administrative Court (capital city only); provincial courts or Tribunais Judicias de Provincia; District Courts or Tribunais Judicias de Districto; customs courts; maritime courts; courts marshal; labor courts; community courts

citizenship.descent: at least one parent must be a citizen of Mozambique

world: has not submitted an ICJ jurisdiction declaration; non-party state to the ICCt
